reviews.text: My visit to the Shanghai Museum was an absolute highlight of my trip, and it stands shoulder-to-shoulder with the great museums of the world. Housed in a stunning architectural masterpiece inspired by an ancient bronze ding vessel, the museum is not just a building but a profound symbol of China's rich cultural heritage. From the moment you step into the grand, circular atrium, you know you are in for something special. The museum's curation is nothing short of masterful. Thematic galleries are arranged over multiple floors, each one a deep dive into a specific art form. The sheer quality and preservation of the artifacts left me speechless. The Ancient Chinese Bronze Gallery is a revelation, showcasing vessels of staggering sophistication and beauty, their intricate designs and inscriptions telling silent stories of power and ritual from millennia ago. The Ceramics Gallery takes you on a breathtaking chronological journey, from the simple elegance of Neolithic pottery to the breathtaking brilliance of Ming and Qing porcelain. Each piece is a testament to unparalleled craftsmanship. Equally impressive were the galleries dedicated to Chinese painting, calligraphy, ancient sculpture, and numismatics. The Minority Nationalities' Art Gallery was a particular surprise and delight, offering a vibrant and colorful perspective on the diverse cultures within China. The exhibits are impeccably displayed with excellent lighting and clear, informative English descriptions that educate without overwhelming. What makes the Shanghai Museum exceptional is its ability to make millennia of history feel immediate and accessible. The flow between galleries is intuitive, the spaces are spacious and serene (even with a good number of visitors), and the staff are courteous and professional. Best of all, this world-class experience is offered free of charge, which is incredibly generous. In summary, the Shanghai Museum is an essential destination for anyone seeking to understand the depth and beauty of Chinese civilization. It is more than a collection of objects; it is a carefully narrated story of artistry, philosophy, and innovation. I spent over four hours captivated and could have easily spent more.

The Shanghai Museum has two buildings: one at People's Square and a newer, larger one called Shanghai Museum East. Admission is free at both, but the reservation process and operating hours differ. People's Square location This is the original building, famous for its unique round-top, square-base architecture that symbolizes the ancient Chinese perception of the world. Located at 201 Renmin Avenue, Huangpu District. Operating hours: 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., closed on Mondays. Admission: Free, but you must reserve a ticket in advance. Highlights: Collections of ancient Chinese art, including bronzes, ceramics, calligraphy, furniture, jades, seals, and paintings. It also features special international exhibitions.

The Shanghai Museum at People's Square has limited displays. During my visit, most of the rooms were closed. However, the building itself is quite impressive. I've heard that there are two or three other branches of the Shanghai Museum nearby that feature more interesting exhibits worth exploring. If you are visiting People's Square, a half-hour visit to the museum is sufficient, and there is generally no waiting time to enter. There's no need to buy tickets; our passports serve as admission.

Slightly crowded but good collection of artefacts e.g traditional wear by different ethnic groups in China, exquisitely carved rhinoceros horn cups, wood furniture. There's a few special exhibition too. Spend approx 2hrs.

I went for the Qipao exhibition. It was very busy inside but there was no waiting/queuing to get into the museum. The exhibition has most of the wall texts in English as well as Mandarin so I had no problem understanding. Entry is free.

For a free museum it was OK, and I think if you had an interest in Chinese history and culture, you would obviously get more out of it. There seemed to be a number of closed exhibits on a lot of the floors when I was there, but I am still glad I made the effort. I walked there from Yu Garden which, knowing now what I didn't know then, I'd just grab a taxi.

上海博物馆 (人民广场馆) The museum is spread over 2 buildings, some distance apart. This is the one at Renmin Square. Free to enter but you need to plan early and snatch tickets online in advance. The slots open at 12.10pm thru their WeChat account 2 wks out (recommend going in at 12nn and keep refreshing the page until it opens). All the slots were snapped up within 20 mins or so. Level 1: A special Egyptian themed exhibit split across 3 halls - The Secrets of Saqqara, The Land of Pharoahs and The Age of Tutankhamun. On till 17 Aug 2025. Wasn't my intent to see this, having been to Saqqara before. But this is what the locals are here for hence the tight ticket situation (cause you first need a general entry into the museum). I paid ¥30 for an audio guide, thinking it was for the normal exhibits, only to realise it's just for the Egyptian showcase. As such, I paid another ¥148 for the ticket to the 3 exhibit halls. The audio guide only covered slightly more than half the exhibits, and with the many tour groups and crowds, it would have been more effective if the earphones are noise-cancelling. Level 3 & 4: Free to enter. A hall on Costumes of the Minority Groups in China, another on Ming Qing Furniture and a special exhibit hall on carvings made out of Rhino horns.

The Shanghai Museum is a remarkable institution that showcases China's rich cultural heritage. Located in the heart of Shanghai, the museum boasts an extensive collection of over 120,000 pieces, including ancient ceramics, jade, bronze, and traditional Chinese paintings. One of its most impressive features is the museum's architecture, designed to resemble a traditional Chinese vessel, symbolizing the concept of "gathering the essence of culture." Inside, the layout is intuitive, allowing visitors to engage with exhibits that are both educational and aesthetically pleasing. The museum does an excellent job of contextualizing artifacts within China's historical timeline, enlightening visitors on the evolution of Chinese art and culture. Additionally, the museum offers a blend of ancient and contemporary exhibits, providing a comprehensive view of China's artistic legacy. Admission is free, making it accessible to a broad audience, enhancing its role as a cultural landmark in Shanghai.

We were asked to book this special exhibition to enter the museum as the free entries to the museum had already sold out. The reservation needs at least a week or two ahead to secure the free entry. If the museum is sold out, do not rush to buy like us. It was utterly crowded and noisy. You could not view a single exhibit in peace. The paid special exhibition were three galleries on ground floor. The price we paid for was a bit hefty. The Chinese galleries were awesome. Go for this if you can get the free entries.
To enter is free. There’s limited display. However it’s still highly recommended.
The part of the meusem in people's square is now much easier to access with no ticket required since 1st September.

Seems like most of the exhibitions have moved over to the new East Museum. Particularly like the exhibition showcasing ancient furniture. Extremely crowded as most were visiting the Civilization of Ancient Egypt exhibition. Please register and make a reservation early before going.

Great museum. I gave only 4 stars, just because it is very hard to reserve entrance ticket for weekend. The ticket is free, but you need to reserve it via museum website. You will need Chinese telephone number for that. They open slots in week before, but all slots for Saturday and Sunday are immediately reserved. I visited this museum twice. My second visit was not so successful: only several halls were open, others were closed for renewing. Very often there is a special exposition on the ground floor, and it could be not free.

Our local travel agent had arranged the entry tickets for us. It was very crowded at the lobby with its temporary Egyptian exhibition. Many of the main collections such as paintings, ceramics, bronze items, jade and seals have already moved to the new building known as Shanghai Museum East in the Pudong area. So we only got to see the sections on furniture, traditional ethnic dress, cloisonne and Persian treasures. The cafe upstairs only served cakes/pastries and drinks. They closed at 5pm sharp.
Interesting place, no entrance fee, multiple zones and floors, located near a subway station.

The Shanghai Museum offered a decent — if not spectacular — experience. Its strength lies in the breadth of its collection: you can wander through galleries dedicated to ancient Chinese bronzes, ceramics, jade, calligraphy, paintings, seals, coins, furniture and more. Among the standouts is the Da Ke ding — a massive Western Zhou-dynasty bronze vessel sometimes called one of China’s “Three Treasures.” For anyone with even a passing interest in Chinese history or art, strolling through those galleries gives a nice sense of the country’s ancient craftsmanship and long cultural arc. That said — and maybe because of the museum’s ambition to be encyclopaedic — the experience can feel a bit overwhelming or even impersonal. With so many categories and so many objects packed in (over 120,000 pieces in many different media), it is hard to deeply connect with each item, especially if you’re on a casual visit rather than a deep-dive art-history mission. I left appreciating the span of history and variety on display — and the “wow” of seeing relics like the Da Ke ding — but didn’t feel the kind of emotional resonance that a more focused, curated exhibition might provoke.

As of April 2025, the main exhibition is "The Civilization of Ancient Egyptian" special exhibition, with many permanent exhibitions relocated to the Pudong branch ("Shanghai Museum East Campus" on Google Maps), leaving only three permanent exhibition halls at the People's Square branch. That's why I spent most of time here on Egyptian exhibitions, the artifacts on display are very well curated with tools, sculptures, tablets, four thousand years old bread, and many historical pieces on display, visualizing the ancient civilization on many aspects. Notes that the names of the exhibits are available in Chinese, English, Japanese, and Korean, but the full description or extended explanation is in Chinese, so make sure your translator app is ready. I spent about an hour at the permanent exhibitions, the displays of Chinese furniture and Chinese minorities' arts and crafts were interesting, but not on the scale that I expected to see here. The permanent exhibition is free, but I couldn't find a way to book the ticket or tell the staff that I just wanted to walk-in. I ended up booking the special exhibition for 148 CNY/person through the "上海博物馆参观预约" WeChat miniapp, just show on your phone that you booked and they will let you in the front entrance, the actual ticket validation is at the entrance of each special exhibition hall using your passport number. Even though I did not expect to see ancient Egyptian artifacts in Shanghai, I believe the special exhibition is worth the price, but this is not the place to learn about Chinese and Shanghai history. If you happen to be in the area, the alternative ones are Shanghai Historical Museum and Shanghai Urban Planning Exhibition Center, both of which are in the People's Square area (disclaimer: I have yet to visit these two).

Free museum on People's Square. According to their website you don't have to reserve on workdays (Tuesday-Friday), but it's very easy so I still recommend to book a time slot to guarantee your visit. I prefer the Shanghai Museum East, but it seems like at the time of my visit some exhibitions were moved from the People's Square location to the East location. It's still worth a visit though.

The Shanghai Museum is an absolute must-visit for anyone interested in Chinese art and culture. With its vast collection of artifacts spanning thousands of years, it's like taking a journey through China's rich history. From ancient ceramics to exquisite jade sculptures, every exhibit showcases the beauty and craftsmanship of Chinese art. Whether you're an art enthusiast or simply curious about China's cultural heritage, the Shanghai Museum offers a captivating experience that's not to be missed.

It has been around ten years since our last visit and we were keen to see the exhibitions. Then, there was a wonderful exhibit showcasing the terracotta warriors. It was an interesting sight to see the building, which is in the shape of an old imperial wine cup traditionally used by the Emperor. Unfortunately, this time, three of the galleries were closed, and the exhibit on Leonardo da Vinci had just ended. Nevertheless, they still had similar galleries showcasing the clothing and jewellery of the minority groups in China, as well as calligraphy and Chinese paintings. We liked the wooden furniture exhibition. All in all, we spent on,y an hour here this time, due to the gallery closures. Entry is free via a QR code, and you need your passport. You can register at the booth outside near the souvenir store, and entry is then further round the corner at the southwest entrance. The nearest Metro exit is number 1.
The Egyptian exhibition is totally worth it, especially the VR experience. But most of the other exhibits have been moved to the museum in Pudong, and only have some furnitures and clothes.

The Egypt exhibition captivates with stunning artifacts, including intricate sarcophagi and exquisite jewelry. Immersive displays bring ancient history to life, while informative panels offer insights into daily life and burial practices. The atmosphere is enriched by ambient sounds, making it a must-see for history enthusiasts and casual visitors alike.

It's a decent place to spend an hour. Quite crowded though as tourists and students alike all come in mass. There were 4 floors but only 2 open exhibits on the 4th floor, 1 open on the 3rd floor, and 1 open on the 1st floor. And the amount of people made it difficult to see an entire exhibit.

A "MUST SEE" FOR VISITORS TO SHANGHAI The Museum is a very well curated collection of amazing items from China's long history. Its free and open every day except Monday. Tour guides will advise that a passport is needed for entry but we were able to enter with no ID at all. You can get a free (English) audio guide - for this you'll need to leave a 400 Yuan refundable deposit (or leave some ID such as drivers licence or ...yes.. your passport!) Its an oasis of cool and quiet and you can easily spend a few hours here marvelling at the age and beauty of the exhibits. Good printed guides in Chinese and English. Guided tours offered but with the audio guide I think you better off doing it yourself and spending time on the things that intrigue you the most. There is a good cafe inside (with good coffee!) and on each floor you will find a souvenir shop with some good (easily packed) treasures to take home :) There is security screening on entry. This museum will not present any problems for people with mobility issues as it has level floors and lifts and escalators. Nearest Metro train station is People's Square (a fair walk just the same which can be tiring in the hot, sticky weather).

This museum is the largest we have visited in Shanghai so far. We spent a whole day there. It has four stories, with entire wings dedicated to chinese bronze, jade, calligraphy, money, ceramics, furniture and Chinese paintings. The most fun part is its gift shop. It has replicas of the exhibits available to purchase (vases, beautiful tea cups, paintings, even bronze containers) if you can afford it.

The Shanghai Museum is a cultural treasure trove. Its vast collection of artifacts, including ancient ceramics, calligraphy, and exquisite artworks, offers a captivating glimpse into China's rich history. The museum's modern architecture and well-curated exhibits make it a must-visit destination for art and history enthusiasts. A journey through time and culture.
Most exhibition have now moved the the west campus, and this information is not available online before visiting.

Look inside the history ofnold times. On the museum are many exhibitions with various things to see as coins, status, pottery and many many more. You will spend here few hours and if you like museums in general this is right place to visit. To know what to expect I put examples of exhibition.

🎭Art & Culture: Beautiful collection of traditional and modern Chinese art and culture. The Shanghai museum is a perfectly preserved capsule of the decades and centuries. The museum is free to enter. There is a paid audio guide that is well worth using. The diverse historical lineage of Chinese tradition is explained extremely well with the voice guide, in your language of choice. The use of different media and historical symbolism of this nation’s artwork, is much deeper than face value. If you enjoy historical museums, this is one to add to your list! The museum was also not terribly crowded which made for a deeply personal experience.

A great museum near people's square. The museum is very well laid out and easily accessible. Good gift shop to pick up a souvenir. Exhibits are diverse with paintings, sculptures, calligraphy, artefacts, furniture, jade and much more. If you are in Shanghai you should stop for a visit, probably 2-3 hours would suffice. Free entry.

This is a great museum to visit if you are touring Shanghai for a few days. It is free to all And located in the beautiful People’s Park. Not a world class museum but it does showcase a nice cross-section of China’s history. I would recommend going to the urban planning museum first if you are pressed for time in Shanghai as it provides an incredible overview of the city past present and future and provides information on each of the historical neighborhoods you can go tour.

Spending time at Shanghai Museum was invaluable. Half day was not enough for someone who's eager to explore the antiques, historic stuffs and arts. Visiting early at the opening time helps you get into the museum quicker and avoid getting stuck in a long queue for more than 1 hour.

Took my two kids there. They were amazed to see some many interesting stuff. A good selection of artefacts - from paintings, calligraphy to furniture, from sculpture to bronze. It's a great place to learn some Chinese Art History. The bilingual display is really helpful for foreigners. We also love the gift shop.

Absolutely terrible ticketing system. It's pretty clear people are just coming here for clout and prestige and that scalpers and group tour companies are swooping in and stealing all the tickets. There's virtually no English language information on how to even get a ticket and once I was able to get on the miniapp via WhatsApp there were several available tickets which were all taken by scalpers immediately while I was attempting to fill my information out for one of them. I doubt they're actually 8,000 people coming in here per the ticket limit and that scalpers in group tour companies are just basically hoarding the tickets for their own profit. Signs nearby at the facility mention this yet they still have this pathetic system. The good news is that there's another museum that actually has Chinese and Asian related artifacts and this is only the special exhibit museum which leads me to believe that people are just coming here for cloud and prestige Rather than caring about the actual exhibitions so they can tick it off their tour itinerary. just a really bad experience because my hotel is down the street from this place and yet after multiple days of trying I couldn't even get in it's booked completely for over a week in advance which is not the case for many landmarks across China which leads me to believe that it's being exploited. Since there's no English language information on how to acquire tickets I posted the actual WeChat program on the attached photo. My advice is to get tickets as soon as a day opens. To add to this, I was I was walking to people's square writing this review when I check the ticketing system again for the exact day when 19 tickets dropped for the exact time slot of the current time which is absolute proof that the system is being exploited and abused.

Massive collection of Chinese history spanning five floors. Furniture, artefacts, and art from China's rich and beautiful culture. Superb examples of the finest ceramics. Everything beautifully displayed and curated.
A treasure box of history with a very nice garden outside with parking space. Museum personnel outside were very patient and helpful to everybody. Very clean toilets. Very interesting Museum Shop.

Interesting and well maintained despite free entrance. While there is no must see unique display or item, I thoroughly enjoy the exhibition here. Was here on weekday afternoon and there is no queue at the entrance. The exhibitions are well organised, and almost all display have English description. Clean restroom and drinking water available on every floor. There's a cafe in second floor if you need a break, else there's benches on every floor but it would mostly be occupied. Definitely one of the best free attraction in Shanghai. Closed on Monday.
During my visit this time, some of the collections were still under repair, but it was enough to observe them for a few hours, which felt good!😊

Big pot shaped building just at the side of famous Peoples Square of Shanghai had enormous collections depicting Chinese history. The building architect was inspired by the priceless big circular tripod pot with two ears bronze vessels called Da Ke Ding from Zhou dynasty (1046-771 BC). Inside of the building looked glistening with granites, marbles & art works. A lot of rooms were exhibiting various periods of Chinese cultures & arts. Basically, it was a modern world class museum in ancient style building showing historical priceless Chinese cultural relics.

The visit is free if you book online in advance, but I found the exhibits and the exhibitions themselves rather poorly designed. Especially when you know how much history China has. In addition, there was hardly any detailed information in languages other than Chinese. The staff also don't speak any foreign languages and can't help visitors from abroad.

A huge museum at the heart of Shanghai, with interesting collections of Chinese history, especially the coinage system! It was free admission on a weekend daytime, and there weren't too many people so I was able to take some time to examine whatever I was interested in. Good place to visit since it's close to the Shanghai landmark, the Bund!
Small collection of historical art and objects from the various dynasties. Free to enter with online reservation. Great time filler if you're on the area.

This is the most hilarious and informative place. I recommend the first floor for a great laugh. Every type of wine cup imaginable - from extra large, too extra small, shaped like a woman, shaped like private parts, shaped like a dog. :D Find out how drunk people were during the time of Confucius! Also exhibits calligraphy, traditional dress (amazing) and sculptures (also amazing). Very informative, free to enter, english maps and self tours available, toilet facilities, wheelchair accessible, paid parking, and 400m from metro exit.

Closed Mondays (except public holidays) as of January 2018 Excellent museum with a large array of Chinese artifacts dating back over a thousand years. Each exhibit is nicely laid out and there are plenty of English explanations.
Nice and well organised museum. I arrived in early so no need to wait at all. Mostly government museum is free but some need id or passport to identify yourself. I love this place. 😊👍
You need to pre-book tickets. We didn't get in. You've been warned! To help you, I've posted the QR code in my photos, so just scan it or Google assistant it.
There was an Egyptian exhibit which was great. Note reserve to get in for free but you must purchase exhibit ticket
Nice museum, composed of multiple exhibitions. Especially nice in the summer heat thanks to the very much appreciated AC. It might take a few minutes to get in due to the usual security check.

Be aware , Monday is holiday in most visiting places so avoid any plans. But, these area are best mentioned and will mesmerise you fullest to core on its view and maintainance. Do explore best flowinring dring season and never miss a opportunity here to visit if you are in shanghaim

It captures the shanghai story in the 1900。some of the artifacts are colorful。other stories relate to the rise of the communist party。the building is huge and provides some quiet time one to think about our past，terrible effects of war。FREE entry
Worth visiting for sure; 4 floors with 4 spacious exhibition halls on each floor. Takes at least 2.5h to see it all without hurry.
One of the best museums in China and outclasses most found in Beijing. Plus it's free! Porcelain and artwork from antiquity as well as furniture from the century.

For travellers, do not come here. This museum is for temporary exhibitions and need specific exhibitions reservations and is very small. Go to Shanghai museum east. It's 10x larger and a must visit.

Really good amount of stuff to see, jam-packed into the many rooms in the museum. You could spend a few hours here, absorbing the history of artefacts and periods. There are extra leaflets that you can pick up in Chinese and English as well. We came here on a tour for one hour and it certainly wasn't long enough.

An totally impressive collection of porcellaines, bronze pcrafts, paintings and coins. The building has the shape of Chinese ancient porcellaines. An afternoon at this place is so illuminating. Wonderful history and experience.
One of the funnest days ever and also saw my favourite NBA player Yao ming which made my year would highly recommend and also a great variety displays.

Great place to visit if you like history and culture. I really enjoyed the museum. The entrance is free and it's also located in a beautiful park. You will feel every bit of history has they have carefully collected and kept each piece.
Not worth going: all the interesting artifacts have been moved to the Shanghai Museum East, which is 30 minutes away. Don't waste your time coming here like I did.

Need to book before coming in. There's no where online to book with foreigner phone as the mini program doesn't work with foreigner Chinese number. You can only book as foreigner with the qr code on the poster in front of the museum. The only available spot today (6 Feb) is for 2 weeks from now (19th Feb). Coming here was a waste of time.

I think this museum is slightly overrated. The museum is not only small but also extremely expensive compared to other museums around the world. I went to see the temporary exhibit about ancient Egypt. The exhibit was small and there not much items. I would rather go to the free British Museum which has a lot more things to explore and learn about. However the VR experience was quite nice, but again requires an extra fee.
Great place to visit if you like history and culture. I really enjoyed the museum. The entrance is free and it's also located in a beautiful park.
Very long queue. The Museum open at 9:00 but if you arrive here around 8:45, you will be able to go inside at 9:30 I love here. Lots of things to see
One of the most visit attraction in Shanghai. They have collected all the ancient Chinese stuffs in very good condition and there are no entry fee! Great place to visit!!!
Lots of antique chairs, tables, currency, ceramics, brush painting. Cool stuff like a replica room of a "dragon" convection pottery furnace and one of the few extant coins minted under Genghis Kahn.
It's great museum to visit and has a variety of collections. You may put your luggage in lobby for free!

Must see in Shanghai. 5 story building with a rich historical collection of chines' art. Galleries include Chinese bronze age, sculptures, ceramic artworks, paintings, calligraphy, seals, furniture, and coins. They could store my suitcase here for me which was great as I was travelling through here.
Majority of the gallery was closed.. if they are open would have been a 5 star museum!
Amazing museum with ancient history pieces along with Chinese artifacts and a lot of interesting and beautiful items.

Amazing collection and facility. Too bad they allow people / kids to misbehave: touching and kissing the glass display, screaming, running around. Total misfit of ancient high civilization and modern uncivilized audience.
It's free to enter so, if there's not a big queue, it's a great place to spend a few minutes or a few hours.

The museum is one of the best in the country and we were fortunate enough to visit while the Egyptian Exhibition was still available. Seriously, please book your tickets online at least a week before. Don’t try your luck and hope to get tickets on actual day. The number of visitors per day is capped and on any given day, the museum is filled to its capacity every hour of opening times.

A must see in Shanghai loved this museum with so much to see inside and so many years of history. Do not miss a visit here if you are in Shanghai. Be careful of people approaching you near here as they try to scam you and take you to a tea house to then rip you off.
A small but sufficient museum. There is no entry fee. The museum can be visited in about 2 hours.

This museum has huge collection of ancient Chinese antiques. The bronze showroom on the ground floor where I spent nearly three hours is the best showroom about Chinese bronze antiques. You can also see how ancient Chinese craftsmen created the bronzes.

It was not possible for tourist from Europe to visit the museum. The staff told me to comeback tomorrow when I will do the online reservation. It turned out it is only possible with WeChat and I don’t have WeChat activated, I am traveling without travel agency, I didn’t know anyone who could activate my WeChat for me. For example The Palace in Beijing, the stuff was profesional there and they were ready to sell the tickets at tickets office without previous reservation. The stuff at Shanghai Museum didn’t help at all.

Shanghai Museum is a world-class museum located in People’s Square, Shanghai, renowned for its extensive collection of ancient Chinese art and artifacts. Established in 1952, it houses over 120,000 pieces, including bronzes, ceramics, paintings, calligraphy, jade, coins, and furniture from various dynasties. The museum’s circular design symbolises ‘heaven and earth’, blending traditional and modern architecture. Admission is free, foreigners might require ticket by producing passport. making it a must-visit for history and culture enthusiasts exploring China’s rich heritage.

They have moved almost all of the exhibitions to the "East Campus"! This older building is not really worth visiting anymore. No reservations needed for off-season half year from September onwards. Entry is free
I came here for a visit from campus. I got a lot point of view and insighrfull when it comes to this museum, especially for making advertisements and promotions
Didn't manage to go in since it seemed reservation needed to enter the place or visit ticket booth first. Too troublesome to enter.

They will tell you it's sold out and that there are no more tickets for a month, and they will send you to a broken online booking site. But if you argue enough, they will give you a ticket—at least, that's what all the foreigners are doing to gain access. It was very frustrating

Excellent collection of a variety of ancient Chinese artifacts dating as far back as the 4th Century B.C. The bronze exhibition is particularly enlightening as it contains some very interesting designs from the 4th-13th centuries that are remarkably intact. The museum does a great job of displaying and explain some of the techniques used to create everything from the moldings to the alloys used. Very intriguing and a great education on early Chinese culture.

Most of the stuff theShanghai Museum was kinda meh. A lot of the exhibits are apparently at their other location now. You have to book tickets online first, which is a bit of a hassle. So, if you're planning a visit, check what's actually on display before you go. It's not bad, just not amazing.

If you don't speak Chinese, I don't recommend trying to gain entrance without a Chinese speaking friend. Entrance is free but you need a reservation to get in. If you just front up to the museum without a reservation you'll need to find the little kiosk near the exit of the gift shop. Here the person will check your passports and give you an entrance time, but they only release a few times every 30 minutes or so (at least that's how it seemed to work). Once you get past that it's pretty straightforward getting in. Our visit was in winter so some of the exhibits were closed for refurbishing. On the plus side that means it wasn't too crowded.

PERMANENT EXHIBITIONS MOVED TO ANOTHER SITE PASSPORT AND AIRLINE TICKET NEEDED FOR ENTRY IF NOT CHINESE, AND RESERVATION IF YOU ARE. This museum now houses temporary exhibitions. Currently a major exhibition in Egypt for another 7 months, and a small one on China and the world at time of Marco Polo with a few Chinese exhibits. There is also a large space for Chinese ethnic costumes largely from late 20th century, furniture, and cloisonné. Other galleries are closed. The bronzes, ceramics, jade, paintings, calligraphy and sculptures have all moved to another brand new site - Shanghai Museum EAST. It’s about 10km away and 25 minutes by hourly (11:00 to 15:00) shuttle bus. (We visited that as well and it’s a truly fantastic no expense spared impressively modern museum). The museum is extremely busy for the Egyptian temporary exhibition and we we repeatedly told we couldn’t enter. In the end we found a hut next to the left of four lions at the front of the museum where our passports and airline tickets were carefully and individually checked and recorded to prove we would be leaving Shanghai before the next reservable entry, and they then issued us free tickets which excluded the Egyptian exhibition. The cafe inside was relatively calm and they do great coffee. A good place to recover after the stress of getting in. The only info we saw about the new site was a small notice outside the closed galleries saying the contents could be seen at the East campus from June 2024.

The Shanghai Museum is a treasure trove of ancient Chinese culture, but few visitors notice its remarkable Feng Shui design. The round dome atop a square base symbolizes “heaven and earth,” harmonizing perfectly with traditional Chinese cosmology. Even the layout of its galleries, which subtly form a spiral, mirrors the concept of infinity—inviting you on an endless journey through time. Another hidden gem is the bronze gallery. If you linger near the large ceremonial ding (ancient cauldron), you might catch faint vibrations—rumored to be the hum of its millennia-old energy. It’s not just an exhibit but an artifact alive with history. Pro tip: Take a close look at the calligraphy gallery. One of the ancient scrolls was mistakenly attributed to a famous poet for centuries until modern analysis revealed it was written by a lesser-known scholar. The Shanghai Museum is a museum of ancient Chinese art, situated on the People's Square in the Huangpu District of Shanghai, China. Rebuilt at its current location in 1996, it is considered one of China's first world-class modern museums. The museum was founded in 1952 and was first open to the public in the former Shanghai Racecourse club house, now at 325 West Nanjing Road. The founding collections came principally from three sources: a batch of artefacts gathered by the Communist 3rd Field Army during the civil war from accidental finds and confiscations of private property and brought to Shanghai upon the Communists' conquest of the city; artefacts confiscated by the customs service; items sold by private collectors due to political pressure during political purges and purchased by the government. The former Shanghai Municipal Museum was also merged into the new Shanghai Museum. The museum has a collection of over 120,000 pieces, including bronze, ceramics, calligraphy, furniture, jades, ancient coins, paintings, seals, sculptures, minority art and foreign art. The Shanghai Museum houses several items of national importance, including one of three extant specimens of a "transparent" bronze mirror from the Han Dynasty.

The Shanghai Museum was founded in 1952. In October 1959, it moved to the old Zhonghui Building, No. 16 Henan South Road. In August 1993, the Shanghai Museum People's Square was opened. On October 12, 1996, it was fully opened. The Shanghai Museum is a large-scale Chinese ancient art museum. Its collection, research, exhibition and education focus on ancient Chinese art. The museum has nearly 1.02 pieces of cultural relics, including more than 140,000 precious cultural relics. The collection of cultural relics of the Shanghai Museum includes 31 categories of bronze, ceramics, paintings, sculptures, oracle bones, embossed, currency, jade, furniture, woven embroidery, lacquerware, bamboo fangs, ethnic cultural relics, etc., especially bronze, ceramics, paintings and calligraphy. Most prominent. The Shanghai Museum has ten art exhibition halls, four cultural relics donation rooms and three special exhibition halls, which reflect the complete development history of various art categories. The system is complete, the collection is rich, and the quality is exquisite. Reputation.

History As a museum of ancient Chinese art, Shanghai Museum possesses a collection of over 1000,000 objects, about 120,000 of which are precious national-graded works of art. Its rich and high-quality collection of ancient Chinese bronze, ceramics, painting and calligraphy is specially celebrated in the world. Founded and first open to the public in the building previously of the horseracing club at 325 W. Nanjing Road in 1952 and then moved into the former Zhonghui Building at 16 S. Henan Road in 1959, the museum developed very quickly in aspects of acquisition, conservation, research, exhibition, education and cultural exchanges with other institutes. In 1992, the Shanghai municipal government allocated to the Museum a piece of land at the very center of the city, the People's Square, as its new site. The whole construction took three years, from August 1993 to its inauguration on October 12th, 1996. The 29.5 meters high new building has a construction space of 39,200 square meters. Its unique architectural form of a round top with a square base, symbolizing the ancient Chinese philosophy that the square earth is under the round sky, is a distinguished architectural combination of traditional feature and modern spirit. The present Shanghai Museum has eleven galleries and three special temporary exhibition halls. It extends warm welcome to the visitors from all over the world.

상하이 여행 필수 코스, 상하이 박물관 방문기 상하이 여행을 하다 보면 화려한 빌딩과 쇼핑거리, 야경이 먼저 떠오르지만 도시의 깊은 역사와 문화를 제대로 느끼고 싶다면 꼭 들러야 할 곳이 바로 상하이 박물관입니다. 상하이 중심부인 인민광장에 위치한 이 박물관은 중국 고대 예술과 문화를 가장 체계적으로 볼 수 있는 곳 중 하나로 꼽히는 유명한 문화 명소입니다. 상하이 박물관 건물 자체도 굉장히 인상적입니다. 위에서 보면 둥근 형태가 얹혀 있는 독특한 구조인데, 중국 전통 사상인 **“하늘은 둥글고 땅은 네모나다(천원지방)”**라는 개념을 건축에 반영한 디자인이라고 합니다. 멀리서 보면 거대한 청동기 솥 같은 느낌도 나는데, 실제로 박물관의 상징 역시 중국 고대 청동 제기인 **정(鼎)**에서 모티브를 따왔다고 합니다. 박물관 내부에 들어가면 규모에 먼저 놀라게 됩니다. 이곳에는 약 백만 점이 넘는 문화재가 소장되어 있으며, 청동기·도자기·옥기·서예·회화·화폐·인장 등 다양한 분야의 중국 고대 유물들이 전시되어 있습니다. 특히 중국 청동기 컬렉션은 세계적으로도 유명한데, 수천 년 전 제사나 의식에 사용되던 거대한 청동 솥과 술잔, 동물 모양 장식들이 매우 정교하게 만들어져 있어 당시 기술과 문화 수준을 짐작하게 합니다. 또 하나 인상적인 전시는 옥(玉) 전시관입니다. 중국에서 옥은 단순한 장신구가 아니라 권위와 순수함을 상징하는 귀한 재료였기 때문에 왕과 귀족들이 사용하던 다양한 옥 장식품과 의례용 유물들이 전시되어 있습니다. 은은한 녹색빛의 옥 장식들을 보고 있으면 중국 고대 문화의 미적 감각을 그대로 느낄 수 있습니다. 도자기 전시도 매우 흥미로운데, 시대별로 다른 색감과 형태의 도자기를 비교하며 보는 재미가 있습니다. 청자, 백자, 채색 도자기 등 중국 도자기 기술이 어떻게 발전해 왔는지 한눈에 이해할 수 있습니다. 상하이 박물관의 또 다른 장점은 입장료가 무료라는 점입니다. 그래서 현지 시민뿐 아니라 세계 각국 관광객들이 많이 방문하는 곳이기도 합니다. 위치도 인민광장 바로 옆이라 난징동루, 신천지, 프랑스 조계지 등 다른 관광지와 함께 여행 코스를 짜기에도 매우 좋습니다. 상하이의 화려한 현대적인 모습 속에서 중국 수천 년의 역사를 조용히 느껴보고 싶다면, 상하이 박물관은 꼭 한 번 방문해볼 가치가 있는 곳입니다. 잠시 시간을 내어 전시를 천천히 둘러보면 상하이라는 도시가 단순한 경제 중심지를 넘어 깊은 문화적 뿌리를 가진 도시라는 것을 느낄 수 있습니다. 상하이 박물관 정보 📍 주소 : Shanghai Museum, 201 Renmin Ave, Huangpu District, Shanghai 🕘 운영시간 : 09:00 ~ 17:00 (월요일 휴관) 💰 입장료 : 무료 #상하이여행 #상하이박물관 #상하이관광 #상하이가볼만한곳 #상하이인민광장 #중국박물관 #상해여행 #상하이여행코스 #중국역사
상하이박물관은 중국 역사를 한눈에 볼 수 있었어. 다양한 전통 도자기부터 고대 청동기, 서예 작품까지 볼 수 있어서 보는 재미가 있어 특히 전시 공간이 넓고 동선도 잘 짜여 있어서 편안하게 관람할 수 있었어. 날씨가 쌀쌀했는데 실내가 쾌적해서 좋았고, 사진 찍기 좋은 포인트도 많아서 추억 남기기 딱 좋았어.

Ouvert en 1952, le musée est organisé en différentes salles répartissant sur trois étages de belles collections où sont exposés environ un million d'objets. On peut trouver, dans le désordre de la calligraphie et des peintures, des sculptures, de la céramique, des objets en bronze, en jade, des sceaux, des meubles, des monnaies et l'art des minorités nationales. Les collection de calligraphie et céramique sont très imposantes avec de beaux objets, rares, que l'on ne voit pas partout. Situé sur la place du Peuple, entièrement gratuit, le musée est ouvert tous les jours de 9h à 17h. Attention, ils ferment les salles progressivement et les entrées ne sont plus permises à partir de 16h. Prévoir 2h minimum pour tout voir, sachant qu'il se peut que des galeries soient fermées lors de votre visite. Un musée qui vaut le détour.

凌晨到上海博物館，來看埃及木乃伊 午夜的鐘聲敲響，我拖著熬夜睏頓的腳步來到上海博物館門口，原以為自己夠瘋狂了，誰會選凌晨零點來看古埃及展？外面雖然有一些人潮，結果一進去到博物館裡面，卻看見滿滿的人潮塞住了. 朋友用手肘撞我： 看！那對穿情侶裝的，男生襯衫印著『法老』，女生是『豔後』，約會約到木乃伊面前，夠硬核！ 我正想笑，卻被檢票員一句話澆了冷水： 您這預約是四天前的凌晨場哦。 心涼半截之際，工作人員掃了眼我們慘白的臉色，跟我們說到服務台改一下日期就可以進去了，快去吧，記得下次別當時間旅行者了。 這份人性化的變通，成了今夜第一個意外暖意。 踏入展廳，薩卡拉秘密展區幽藍的光籠罩著人群。本該寂靜的凌晨一點，這裡卻流動著壓低的驚嘆聲。 手機電筒貼著展櫃細照一串項鍊： 瞧這聖甲蟲鑲嵌的方位，代表太陽神重生之力，少年眼中閃著求知的光，哪有半分睡意？轉角遇見 古埃及眾神巡遊 ，貓女神頂著金冠甩動裙擺，鷹頭神荷魯斯遞來象形文字謎題卡，傳說中的法老王與豔後蹤影全無，倒是層疊的彩繪棺槨森然列陣。旁邊展櫃忽現詭萌之物：巴掌大的亞麻布包裹蜷成團，標籤寫著 貓木乃伊 。原來古埃及人奉貓為神，將寵物製成木乃伊獻祭，纏裹之精緻堪比人類，只為取悅獅首女身的芭絲特女神。 凌晨兩點半，悵然於未睹法老真容的我們晃到二樓。濃郁咖啡香襲來——天！落地窗邊滿座！白領敲著筆電配紅絲絨蛋糕，情侶分食撒金粉的巧克力金字塔，阿姨們舉手機拍拉花： 這杯栗博拿鐵的拉花是歷史博物館鐘樓呢！ 最絕的是櫥窗裡一座 青銅鼎 ，服務生笑道： 鼎是巧克力脆殼，裡面填提拉米蘇，上博鎮館之寶變甜點！ 這一夜，上海人把凌晨過成了白晝。有人為追文明微光，有人貪戀深夜咖啡座，更有人單純享受這魔幻時空，當博物館打破 朝九晚五 的枷鎖，當木乃伊與拿鐵同在星空下醒著，這座城便永遠生猛。 #上海博物館 #金字塔之巔：古埃及文明大展 #上海

II Museo di Shangha è un museo di arte cinese antica situato a Puxi sulla Piazza del popolo di Shanghai nel distretto di Huangpu. É uno dei musei più importanti di tutta la Cina. Inoltre, l'ingresso è gratuito, per cui merita sicuramente una visita.

这座建筑由本土建筑师邢同和设计，1996年开放。建筑造型刻意为之——仿照古代青铜鼎的形制，方基圆顶，象征中国传统宇宙观"天圆地方"。据说设计灵感来源于馆内展出的大克鼎。但这算哪门子后现代主义的平庸之作？网格穹顶天窗、华夫格吊顶、到处都是花岗岩——与其说是古代艺术的珍宝盒，不如说更像一座故作深沉的机场航站楼。 话虽如此，馆藏确实令人印象深刻。少数民族服饰展厅让我眼前一亮——那些刺绣丝绒袍子和精致的三寸金莲绣鞋都很惊艳。明清家具展厅更是精彩绝伦，透过典雅的月洞门可以欣赏各式珍品。有些藏品看起来价值不菲，尤其是那尊蓝色火焰纹、金色鬃毛的景泰蓝狮子香炉。 亮点： 免费入场——这点很赞。多层中庭气势恢宏，交叉楼梯颇具戏剧性。工作日上午展厅很安静。 小缺点： 礼品店销售人员有点过于热情，而且礼品店正好设在出口必经之路上。周四上午10:15左右离开时，人流开始增多，但展厅内依然清静。 如果你在人民广场附近，值得花一上午来逛逛。建议早点到。

中国の壮大な歴史を体感できるという上海博物館を訪れてみました。この博物館は人民広場にあり、古代の青銅器や陶磁器、書画など、膨大な数の文物が展示されていることで有名ですね。特に青銅器のコレクションは、世界的に見ても素晴らしいと聞いていたので、とても楽しみにしていました。 しかし、実際に来てみると、入場方法が少し複雑でした。まず、事前に予約が必要なんですね。オンラインで予約を試みましたが、中国の電話番号が必要なようで、私はうまくいきませんでした。外国人旅行者は、パスポートを持参して、通常の入り口から少し西へ行ったところにあるチケット・インフォメーションカウンターに行けば、無料のチケットがもらえるようです。ただ、これを知らないと私のように無駄足になってしまうので、これから行く方は注意してください。 それから、もう一つ残念だったのは、多くの展示品が郊外にある東館に移設されていたことです。特に楽しみにしていた青銅器や陶磁器の多くがそちらに移ってしまったと聞いて、少しがっかりしました。そのため、じっくりと時間をかけて見たい方は、最初から東館を訪れることをお勧めします。 とはいえ、無料で見学できるという点は素晴らしいと思います。もし、時間があって人民広場周辺に来ることがあれば、足を運んでみるのも良いかもしれませんね。ただし、休日はかなり混雑するようなので、平日に行くか、開館時間に合わせて早めに行くのが良さそうです。

Attenzione ai giorni di maggior afflusso perché il numero di visitatori disponibili per una giornata è limitato. Shanghai Museum si sviluppa su quattro piani. Il primo piano è dedicato a sculture e oggetti, soprattutto in bronzo, risalenti anche al 5000 a.C. Un dettaglio: se si vuole approfittare del ristorante (buono, economico e situato sempre al primo piano) occorre farsi dare un braccialetto che permette di uscire e rientrare dalla zona controlli senza fare nuovamente tutta la fila. Il secondo piano presenta innanzitutto esposizioni di ceramiche. Al terzo piano si possono trovare sale espositive dove poter ammirare dipinti tradizionali, sigilli e una mostra di calligrafia. Per finire il quarto piano offre la possibilità di visitare uno spazio con abiti, maschere e oggettistica, tipici delle minoranze etniche di questo Paese. Poi una sala espositiva con oggetti ottenuti dalla lavorazione della giada, uno spazio dedicato alle monete e infine una sala con mobili, panche e sedie in legno, lavorato e cesellato con grande maestria, appartenuti all’epoca Ming e Qing. Per una visita piuttosto superficiale si può impiegare anche un’ora e mezza. Altrimenti è auspicabile dedicarvi almeno mezza giornata, magari con l’ausilio di un’audioguida disponibile al desk del primo piano. Se si passa da Shanghai questo Museo è da visitare assolutamente!

Museum ShanghaiTerletak di People's Square , Distrik Huangpu , Shanghai. Ini adalah museum seni rupa Tionghoa kuno yang sangat terkenal dan memiliki koleksi yang lengkap. Dibangun ulang di lokasi saat ini pada 1996, museum tersebut dianggap sebagai salah satu museum modern kelas dunia pertama di Tiongkok. Museum ini memiliki lebih dari 120.000 buah koleksi, yang terbuat dari perunggu , keramik , kaligrafi , furnitur , batu giok , koin kuno , lukisan , segel , patung dan lain lain. Museum Shanghai menyimpan beberapa barang penting nasional, termasuk satu dari tiga spesimen cermin perunggu "transparan" dari Dinasti Han yang masih ada. Gaya dan penyajiannya mengelilingi pengunjung dengan artefak yang menunjukkan kearifan dan filosofi kuno. Desain eksterior kubah bundar dan alas persegi melambangkan gagasan kuno tentang surga bundar dan tanah persegi. Museum ini terbagi menjadi 11 galeri dan 3 ruang pameran. 11 galeri mencakup sebagian besar hasil seni Tiongkok yang utama : Perunggu Kuno, Keramik Kuno, Lukisan, Kaligrafi, Patung Kuno, Giok Kuno, Koin, Furnitur Ming dan Qing, Segel, dan Kebangsaan Minoritas. Lebih dari 500 karya adalah karya seni dari berbagai dinasti, seperti tembikar dicat abu-abu dari zaman Neolitik, celadon primitif dari Shang, Zhou dan Negara Berperang, seladon dewasa dari Dinasti Han Timur, tembikar kaca tiga warna yang terkenal dari Dinasti Tang, kaca biru, putih dan hitam serta porselen yang dicat dari Song, Jin dan Liao, dan karya dari Jingdezhen, Jiangxi dll. Untuk menuju museum ini dapat ditempuh dengan transportasi umum sebagai berikut : Dengan metro: Naik Metro Jalur 1 , Jalur 2 , atau Jalur 8 dan turun di People's Square Station. Keluar dari stasiun dari Exit 1 dan berjalanlah ke selatan selama sekitar lima menit. Dengan bus: 1. Naik bus 46, 49, 123, 145, 312, 451 atau Jalur Khusus Shangchuan dan turun di People's Square Station. 2. Naik Bus Wisata Kota Jalur 1 atau Jalur 2 dan turun di museum. 3. Ambil Tunnel Line 6 dan turun di Stasiun Wushenglu Xizang Zhonglu.

El Museo de Shanghai está dedicado al arte chino antiguo. Se encuentra en la Plaza del Pueblo, en el distrito de Huangpu de la municipalidad de Shanghái, en la República Popular China. El museo abrió por primera vez sus puertas en el año 1952 en un edificio modernista de la calle Nanjing. Posteriormente (1959) se trasladó a la calle Henan. El museo actual se inauguró en el año 1996. El edificio que alberga el museo tiene forma circular y ocupa un área de 39.200 m² de los que más de 10.000 están dedicados a exposiciones. Su altura es de 29,5 metros, divididos en cinco pisos. Diseñado por un arquitecto local, el edificio tiene una forma circular sobre una base cuadrada, simbolizando así la antigua percepción china del mundo: Un cielo redondo, una tierra cuadrada. El museo contiene una colección de más de 120.000 piezas, divididas en diez categorías diferentes: bronce, escultura, cerámica, jade, pintura, caligrafía, sellos, monedas, muebles de las dinastías Ming y Qing y artes de las minorías chinas.

上海博物馆创建于1952年，原址南京西路325号旧跑马总会，1959年10月迁入河南南路16号中汇大楼，现址上海市中心人民广场的南侧黄浦区人民大道201号。 1993年8月，上海博物馆新馆开工建设，1996年10月12日全面建成开放。上海博物馆建筑总面积39200平方米，占地面积1.1万平方米，地下二层，地上五层，高29.5米，总投资5.7亿元。新馆是方体基座与圆形出挑相结合的建筑造型，具有中国“天圆地方”的寓意。馆名“上海博物馆”为上海第一任市长陈毅书写。 上海博物馆设有11个专馆，3个展览厅，陈列面积2,800平方米。馆藏文物近百万件，其中精品文物12万件，其中尤其是以青铜器、陶瓷器、书法、绘画为特色。收藏了来自宝鸡及河南、湖南等地的青铜器，有文物界“半壁江山”之誉，是一座大型的中国古代艺术博物馆，故此很值得一看！ The Shanghai Museum was founded in 1952. It was originally located at the Old Race Club at No. 325 Nanjing West Road. It moved into the Zhonghui Building at No. 16 Henan South Road in October 1959. It is now located at No. 201, Renmin Avenue, Huangpu District, on the south side of the People's Square in the central Shanghai. In August 1993, the construction of the new Shanghai Museum started, and it was fully opened on October 12, 1996. The Shanghai Museum has a total building area of ​​39,200 square meters, covering an area of ​​11,000 square meters, with two floors underground and five floors above ground, with a height of 29.5 meters and a total investment of 570 million yuan. The new pavilion is an architectural shape that combines a square base with a round overhang, which has the meaning of "a place with a round sky" in China. The name "Shanghai Museum" was written by Chen Yi, the first mayor of Shanghai. The Shanghai Museum has 11 special halls, 3 exhibition halls, and an exhibition area of ​​2,800 square meters. The museum has nearly one million cultural relics, including 120,000 fine cultural relics, especially bronze ware, ceramics, calligraphy, and paintings. It has a collection of bronzes from Baoji, Henan, Hunan and other places. It is known as the "half of the country" in the cultural relic world. It is a large-scale ancient Chinese art museum.

中国の歴史を感じることができる博物館。 膨大な人口の中国なうえにこの大規模な博物館が無料というだけあって入場するだけでも数分並びます。 博物館の常設展示はそれぞれの展示内容ごとに部屋がわかれており、分野ごとにその歴史を学んでいくことができます。 開館時間は9:00から17:00ですが内容量はそれ以上あると感じました。 言語がわからなくても視覚的にわかるものもありますが、各展示の入り口に展示案内の紙が置かれてあるのでそれを手に取って見回ればある程度のことは把握できると思います。 また、一階に音声ガイドのレンタルもあるのでそちらでレンタルすることでさらに理解を深めることが可能だと思います。

上海博物館是中國最著名的博物館之一，館藏文物豐富，展覽精彩，是上海的一大文化地標。 上海博物館的優點主要體現在以下幾個方面： **館藏文物豐富：**上海博物館館藏文物14萬餘件，包括青銅器、陶瓷、玉器、書畫、雕塑、漆器、金銀器、工藝美術品等，涵蓋中國古代各個歷史時期和各個門類，是中國最全面、最系統的古代文物收藏機構之一。 **展覽精彩：**上海博物館每年舉辦多場大型展覽，涵蓋中國古代藝術、世界文明、自然科學等領域，展覽內容豐富多彩，展覽形式新穎多樣，深受廣大觀眾喜愛。 **服務周到：**上海博物館的服務人員態度友好，熱情周到，為觀眾提供優質的參觀服務。 總而言之，上海博物館是中國古代藝術的寶庫，是上海的文化地標，是值得一去再去的博物館。
